name: mira
label: Mira (omicron Cet A, M7 IIIe long-period variable)
sources: Woodruff et al. 2004, A&A 421, 703 (VLTI/VINCI, K band): Rosseland diameter 28.9 +/- 0.3 mas at phase 0.13 to 34.9 +/- 0.4 mas at phase 0.40; T_eff 3192 -> 2918 K
van Leeuwen 2007: parallax 10.91 +/- 1.22 mas (92 pc, 11 %); GCVS: V 2.0-10.1, period 332 d, mean maximum ~3.5; mass ~1 Msun (Zamanov et al. 2026); Mira B at 0.49 arcsec (negligible light)
notes: theta_ld_mas 32 mas is the 900 nm near-continuum size near maximum light, ASSUMED between the K-band Rosseland values; the optical TiO-band diameters are larger (40-50 mas), which the optional 650 nm night and the chromatic_diameter table represent.
The diameter changes by +/- 10 % over the 332 d pulsation and the star by 7 mag: the forecast is for nights near maximum, not a light-curve model; one night at 900 nm on a 2.5+3 m line gives ~2 %.
First null at 900 nm: 7.1 m (3.5 m at 650 nm for the 45 mas TiO disk).
Anchors are Vega magnitudes converted with the band table's Vega -> AB offsets (V +0.02, H +1.39, K +1.85).
The radius is derived from theta_LD and the distance.
assumptions: theta_ld_mas (32 mas at 900 nm near maximum)
